question.problem:
Which of the three sequences below are arithmetic sequences?

I. $13,\,6,\,-1,\,-9,...$

II. $13,\,19,\,25,\,31,...$

III. $13,\,39,\,117,\,351,...$
question.worked_solution:
To determine whether each sequence is an arithmetic sequence, we need to look at the jumps between terms in the sequence. If the jumps are the same, then they indeed represent a common difference of an arithmetic sequence.

- In sequence I, the jumps are not all the same. Therefore, sequence I is not an arithmetic sequence.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14261220/assets/807549580ce3c6d83ac3a0e6b53e127d60197ec16ccf99fd1499928c0437882c.png)

- In sequence II, the jumps are all the same. Therefore, sequence II is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d=6.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14261220/assets/77ce359fc2a02a86db5aafc4b665b14edd9425142ab4e77df6ced0880489d56b.png)

- In sequence III, the jumps are not all the same. Therefore, sequence III is not an arithmetic sequence either.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14261220/assets/059f0c7009a43990d4b742ddc8b57b357fa2cd23b037ad5136f3121f2c62a036.png)

In conclusion, only sequence II is an arithmetic sequence.
